prs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds a proposed timeline and budget section to the roadmap. These estimates are presented as **one proposal for discussion**, not a final plan.

### Proposed:
- **Timeline**: 18 months across 6 phases
- **Personnel**: ~1.5 FTE (Max 60%, Ben 50%, John 30%)
- **Budget**: ~$270,000-370,000

### Alternative scenarios included:
- Accelerated (12 months)
- Extended (24 months)  
- MVP (9 months)

## Context

This content was separated from the main roadmap to allow the methodology and phasing to be reviewed independently from timeline/budget assumptions. The "Open Questions for Planning" section in master frames the key decisions that need discussion before finalizing these estimates.

## Questions for discussion

1. Does the 18-month timeline reflect realistic expectations given AI-assisted development?
2. Is the personnel allocation appropriate, or should we consider different team structures?
3. Should we pursue a planning grant first to align on approach before full funding?
4. How does existing PolicyEngine infrastructure (SSI, SNAP, etc. already implemented) change the scope estimate?

prs.title: Add blog post: The SALT Torpedo and Charitable Giving
prs.body:
## Summary
- Adds new blog post analyzing how the SALT cap phase-out affects charitable giving incentives
- Key finding: a $700k earner pays $1,928 more for a $10k donation than a $300k earner
- Embeds interactive Plotly charts from https://policyengine.github.io/salt-torpedo-giving/

The analysis reveals that the SALT cap phase-out in OBBBA (which reduces the cap from $40k to $10k for high earners) pushes many high-income filers to take the standard deduction instead of itemizing. When they donate, they switch to itemizing but only get partial benefit because they lose the "free" standard deduction.

- Generate all stochastic boolean take-up decisions
- Use seeded RNG (seed=100) for full reproducibility

## Summary

Fixes invalid `filing_status` enum values in test files that were silently converted to `SINGLE` (index 0) due to a bug in policyengine-core (see [#410](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-core/issues/410)).

These invalid values didn't cause test failures because `numpy.select()` in `Enum.encode()` returns 0 (the default) when no condition matches, silently converting invalid values to the first enum value.

prs.title: Fix silent data corruption for invalid enum values
prs.body:
## Summary

Invalid enum values passed to `Enum.encode()` were silently converted to index 0 (the first enum value) instead of raising an error. This caused silent data corruption in simulations.

## The Problem

In `Enum.encode()`, `numpy.select()` is used to map string values to enum indices:

```python
array = numpy.select(
    [array == item.name for item in cls],
    [item.index for item in cls],
)
```

When no condition matches (invalid value), `numpy.select` returns its default value of `0`, which silently converts invalid values to the first enum item.

For example:
- `'MARRIED'` passed to `FilingStatus` (which has `SINGLE`, `JOINT`, `SEPARATE`) would silently become `SINGLE` (index 0)
- Empty string `''` would also silently become the first enum value

## Real-World Impact

This bug was discovered in [PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#6901](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/6901) where Missouri test files had:
- `filing_status: MARRIED` (invalid - should be `JOINT`)
- `filing_status: ` (empty/blank)

These tests passed silently because the invalid values were converted to `SINGLE`.

## The Fix

Add validation after `numpy.select` to detect unmatched values and raise a descriptive error:

```python
unmatched_mask = ~numpy.isin(original_array, valid_names)
if unmatched_mask.any():
    invalid_values = numpy.unique(original_array[unmatched_mask])
    raise ValueError(
        f"Invalid value(s) {invalid_values.tolist()} for enum "
        f"{cls.__name__}. Valid values are: {valid_names}"
    )
```

## Test Plan

- Added `tests/core/test_enum_encoding.py` with tests for:
  - Valid single values encode correctly
  - Valid multiple values encode correctly
  - Invalid values raise ValueError with helpful message
  - Empty strings raise ValueError
  - Mixed valid/invalid values raise ValueError
  - Case sensitivity is enforced
  - Order is preserved in encoding

Fixes #410

reviews.title: Add UK Gift Aid support with PolicyEngine-UK
reviews.body:
## Summary

This PR adds UK tax calculation support to GiveCalc, enabling UK users to calculate the tax impact of charitable donations via Gift Aid.

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:** [PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk#1430](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk/pull/1430) - Fix Gift Aid Personal Allowance taper interaction

This PR depends on the policyengine-uk fix for Gift Aid PA taper calculation. Once that PR is merged and released, the policyengine-uk version constraint here can be updated.

## Changes

### New UK Module (`givecalc/uk/`)
- `constants.py`: UK-specific constants (tax year, regions)
- `situation.py`: Creates PolicyEngine-UK situations with donation axes
- `tax.py`: UK tax calculations (marginal savings, donation effects)

### API Endpoints (`api/main.py`)
- `GET /api/uk/regions`: List UK regions grouped by nation
- `GET /api/uk/tax-programs`: Gift Aid program information  
- `POST /api/uk/calculate`: Calculate UK tax impact of Gift Aid donations

### Schemas (`api/schemas.py`)
- `UKIncomeInput`, `UKCalculateRequest`, `UKCalculateResponse`
- `UKRegionInfo`, `UKRegionsResponse`
- `UKDonationDataPoint`, `UKTaxProgramsResponse`

### Dependencies
- Added `policyengine-uk>=2.45.0,<2.55.0` (Python 3.12 compatible)
- Includes workaround for policyengine-uk dataset attribute bug (fixed in 2.55.0+ which requires Python 3.13+)

## UK Tax System Details

Gift Aid provides tax relief in two ways:
1. **Charity reclaim**: Charities reclaim 25p per £1 donated (basic rate relief at 20%)
2. **Donor relief**: Higher rate (40%+) taxpayers claim additional relief personally

Example for a £100 donation by a 40% taxpayer:
- Charity receives: £100 + £25 (basic rate reclaim) = £125
- Donor claims: £25 (difference between 40% and 20% on £125 gross)
- Net cost to donor: £75

Supports all UK regions including Scotland (with different income tax rates).

## Testing

47 new tests covering:
- UK situation creation (18 tests)
- UK tax calculations (14 tests)
- UK API endpoints (13 tests)

All 80 tests pass (existing + new).

Closes #58 (parent issue)

reviews.title: Add owns vehicle variable
reviews.body:
Summary

Adds a new owns_vehicle input variable to support calibration of vehicle ownership rates in policyengine-uk-data.

  This addresses https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk-data/issues/236, which identified that the  microdata shows 54.1% of households with zero fuel spending, while NTS 2024 data shows only 22% of UK households lack a car - a 32 percentage point gap.

  Changes

  - Added owns_vehicle boolean input variable at household level

  How it works

This is an input variable (no formula). The value will be imputed in policyengine-uk-data based on LCFS fuel spending data (households with petrol/diesel spending are assumed to own a vehicle), then calibrated to NTS 2024 targets (~78% vehicle ownership).

  This approach:
  - Keeps the relationship between vehicle ownership and fuel spending in the data layer, not the tax-benefit system
  - Allows proper calibration/reweighting
  - Handles EVs correctly (they can be assigned owns_vehicle=True without fuel spending)

  References

  - https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/national-travel-survey-2024/nts-2024-household-car-availability-and-trends-in-car-trips
  - https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6781339100e3d719f19217f1/dft-car-ownership-evidence-review.pdf

reviews.title: Optimise import and microsimulation init performance
reviews.body:
Three changes that together reduce `from policyengine_uk import Microsimulation; sim = Microsimulation()` time by ~40% (10.75s → 6.6s):

**Enum encoding** - replaced `np.select` with `np.searchsorted` for O(n log m) lookup instead of O(n*m), with cached sorted lookup arrays via `@lru_cache`

**empty_clone** - replaced dynamic type creation with `object.__new__()` which is ~33x faster for the 32k calls during parameter cloning

**Period/instant parsing** - added `@lru_cache` to `_instant_from_string` and `_period_from_string` to avoid repeated `strptime` calls for the same period strings (called ~20k times during fiscal year parameter conversion)

Remaining bottlenecks are mostly inherent to data loading (`astype` at 0.80s, HuggingFace dataset at 0.82s) rather than algorithmic inefficiencies.

issues.title: TAXSIM-35 does not enforce age 25 minimum for childless EITC
issues.body:
## Summary

TAXSIM-35 does not enforce the age eligibility requirement for childless EITC claimants. Per 26 USC § 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(II), a childless filer must be between ages 25 and 64 to claim EITC.

## Reproduction

```python
# Age 23 childless filer with $8,000 earned income
# Expected: $0 (ineligible due to age)
# TAXSIM returns: $599.65

Input: page=23, depx=0, pwages=8000, year=2023
Output: v25 (EITC) = 599.65
```

The `page` (primary taxpayer age) variable is correctly passed to TAXSIM, but TAXSIM ignores it for EITC eligibility and calculates the credit based purely on income and number of children.

## Impact

This affects validation comparisons between PolicyEngine and TAXSIM for childless filers under 25 or over 64. PolicyEngine correctly applies the age test and returns $0, while TAXSIM returns a non-zero credit.

## Workaround

When comparing PolicyEngine vs TAXSIM results, filter out test cases where:
- `qualifying_children == 0` AND (`age < 25` OR `age > 64`)

## Reference

- Statute: [26 USC § 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(II)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32)
- TAXSIM docs: https://taxsim.nber.org/taxsim35/

issues.title: Restore monorepo split: separate calculator (app.policyengine.org) and website (policyengine.org)
issues.body:
## Summary

Re-implement the monorepo split that was reverted due to production issues. The goal is to deploy:
- **app.policyengine.org** → Calculator app (policy simulations, household builder)
- **www.policyengine.org** → Website (homepage, blog, team, research)

## What Was Built (PR #494, reverted)

### Architecture
- Turborepo monorepo with npm workspaces
- `@policyengine/design-system` package for shared tokens/components
- Separate entry points: `CalculatorApp.tsx`, `WebsiteApp.tsx`
- Separate HTML files: `calculator.html`, `website.html`
- `VITE_APP_MODE` environment variable controls which app to build
- Three Vercel projects connected to same repo:
  - `policyengine-calculator` → app.policyengine.org
  - `policyengine-website` → www.policyengine.org
  - `policyengine-app-v2` → legacy combined build

### Key Files Created
- `vercel.json` - Website project config
- `vercel.calculator.json` - Calculator project config
- `packages/design-system/` - Shared design tokens
- `app/src/CalculatorRouter.tsx` - Calculator routes
- `app/src/WebsiteRouter.tsx` - Website routes
- `app/src/CalculatorApp.tsx` - Calculator app with all providers
- `app/src/WebsiteApp.tsx` - Website app with all providers

---

## Postmortem: What Went Wrong

### Root Cause: Deployed Unreviewed Code to Production Domains

**The site broke BEFORE the PR was even merged.** The mistake was using `vercel alias set` to point production domains at deployments from an unmerged feature branch.

Actions that broke production:
```bash
vercel --prod --scope policy-engine           # Deployed feature branch
vercel alias set <deployment> www.policyengine.org   # Pointed PRODUCTION at it
vercel alias set <deployment> app.policyengine.org   # Pointed PRODUCTION at it
```

The correct approach would have been:
```bash
vercel --scope policy-engine                  # Deploy to preview URL (no --prod)
# Test at preview URL: https://policyengine-website-xxxxx.vercel.app
# Only after PR merge does production update automatically
```

### Secondary Issue: Missing Providers
The `WebsiteApp.tsx` was initially created without required React context providers (Redux, QueryClient), causing runtime errors. But this would have been caught during PR review if we'd tested the preview URL instead of pushing to production.

### Timeline
1. PR #494 created with monorepo split code
2. **Production domains pointed at feature branch deployments** - bypassing PR review
3. Site immediately showed React errors
4. Team noticed production was running from `monorepo-split` branch before PR was merged
5. Decision made to revert to restore service

---

## Required Controls Before Re-implementing

### 1. **Vercel CLI Protocol & Verification Script**

Create a verification script to run before ANY manual Vercel CLI changes that affect production:

```bash
# scripts/verify-vercel-deployment.sh
#!/bin/bash
set -e

DEPLOY_URL=$1

if [ -z "$DEPLOY_URL" ]; then
  echo "Usage: ./verify-vercel-deployment.sh <deployment-url>"
  exit 1
fi

echo "🔍 Verifying deployment: $DEPLOY_URL"

# 1. Check HTTP 200
echo "Checking HTTP status..."
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$DEPLOY_URL")
if [ "$STATUS" != "200" ]; then
  echo "❌ FAILED: HTTP status $STATUS (expected 200)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ HTTP 200 OK"

# 2. Check for React error indicators
echo "Checking for React errors..."
BODY=$(curl -s "$DEPLOY_URL")
if echo "$BODY" | grep -q "Unexpected Application Error"; then
  echo "❌ FAILED: React error boundary triggered"
  exit 1
fi
if echo "$BODY" | grep -q "Cannot destructure property"; then
  echo "❌ FAILED: Provider/context error detected"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ No React errors detected"

# 3. Check key elements exist
echo "Checking page structure..."
if ! echo "$BODY" | grep -q "<title>PolicyEngine</title>"; then
  echo "❌ FAILED: Missing expected title"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ Page structure OK"

# 4. Check key routes (fetch a few paths)
for path in "/" "/us" "/uk"; do
  ROUTE_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$DEPLOY_URL$path")
  if [ "$ROUTE_STATUS" != "200" ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Warning: Route $path returned $ROUTE_STATUS"
  else
    echo "✅ Route $path OK"
  fi
done

echo ""
echo "✅ All checks passed for $DEPLOY_URL"
echo ""
echo "⚠️  BEFORE aliasing to production:"
echo "   1. Manually test the deployment in a browser"
echo "   2. Check console for JavaScript errors"
echo "   3. Test key user flows (homepage, calculator)"
echo "   4. Get team sign-off if this is a major change"
```

**Protocol for manual Vercel changes:**

1. Deploy to preview (no `--prod`): `vercel --scope policy-engine`
2. Run verification: `./scripts/verify-vercel-deployment.sh <preview-url>`
3. Manually test in browser
4. For major changes, get team sign-off
5. Only then alias to production (if needed outside of normal Git flow)

### 2. Pre-merge Verification
- [ ] **Mandatory preview URL check** - Before merging PRs that touch app entry points, manually verify the Vercel preview loads without errors
- [ ] **Add PR template checkbox**: "I have verified the Vercel preview URL loads correctly"

### 3. Automated E2E Smoke Tests in CI
- [ ] Add Playwright or Cypress test that:
  - Loads the app
  - Verifies no React error boundary is triggered
  - Checks that key routes render
- [ ] Run against Vercel preview URL in CI

### 4. Integration Tests for App Entry Points
- [ ] Add tests that render `CalculatorApp` and `WebsiteApp` fully (not mocked)
- [ ] Verify all required providers are present

### 5. Monitoring
- [ ] Set up error monitoring (Sentry) to catch React errors quickly
- [ ] Alert on error rate spikes

---

## Vercel Cleanup Needed

The following were created and may need cleanup:
- Vercel project: `policyengine-calculator` 
- Vercel project: `policyengine-website`
- DNS record in Squarespace: `app` CNAME → `cname.vercel-dns.com`
- Domain alias: `app.policyengine.org`

---

## Implementation Plan (When Ready)

1. **Create verification script** - `scripts/verify-vercel-deployment.sh`
2. **Add E2E smoke tests to CI** - Before any split work
3. **Fix and test both apps** - Using preview URLs only
4. **Run verification script** - On preview deployments
5. **Get team sign-off** - Before any production changes
6. **Merge PR** - Let Vercel Git integration handle production deployment
7. **Monitor** - Watch for errors after merge

---

## Key Lessons

1. **Always test on preview URLs first** - Vercel gives every deployment a unique URL
2. **Run verification script before production changes** - Automated sanity checks catch obvious failures
3. **Don't point production domains at unreviewed code** - Even if tests pass, get human verification

---

## Related

- Reverted PR: #494
- Branch with work: `monorepo-split`
- Vercel projects created: `policyengine-calculator`, `policyengine-website`

issues.title: Silent data corruption: Invalid enum values default to index 0 instead of raising error
issues.body:
## Summary

When an invalid enum value is passed to a variable (e.g., `filing_status: MARRIED` when valid values are `SINGLE`, `JOINT`, etc.), the value is **silently converted to index 0** (the first enum value) instead of raising an error.

This is a critical bug that can lead to incorrect simulation results without any warning.

## Root Cause

In `policyengine_core/enums/enum.py`, the `encode()` method uses `numpy.select()` to convert string values to enum indices:

```python
array = numpy.select(
    [array == item.name for item in cls],
    [item.index for item in cls],
).astype(ENUM_ARRAY_DTYPE)
```

When no condition matches (invalid value), `numpy.select` returns its default value of `0`, which silently converts invalid values to the first enum item.

## Example

```python
# FilingStatus enum has: SINGLE (0), JOINT (1), SEPARATE (2), HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD (3), SURVIVING_SPOUSE (4)

# This should raise an error but instead silently becomes SINGLE (index 0)
simulation.set_input("filing_status", "2024", ["MARRIED"])  

# This also silently becomes SINGLE
simulation.set_input("filing_status", "2024", [""])  
```

## Real-World Impact

This bug was discovered in [PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#6901](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/6901) where Missouri test files had:
- `filing_status: MARRIED` (invalid - should be `JOINT`)
- `filing_status: ` (empty/blank)

These tests passed silently because the invalid values were converted to `SINGLE`.

## Proposed Fix

Modify the `encode()` method to detect unmatched values and raise a descriptive error:

```python
# After numpy.select, check for default values that indicate unmatched inputs
if isinstance(original_array, numpy.ndarray) and original_array.dtype.kind in {"U", "S"}:
    unmatched_mask = ~numpy.isin(original_array, [item.name for item in cls])
    if unmatched_mask.any():
        invalid_values = numpy.unique(original_array[unmatched_mask])
        valid_values = [item.name for item in cls]
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid enum value(s) {invalid_values.tolist()} for {cls.__name__}. "
            f"Valid values are: {valid_values}"
        )
```

## Severity

**Critical** - This causes silent incorrect calculations without any warning, which is worse than a crash.

issues.title: Use April dates for uprating indices to align with UK fiscal year
issues.body:
## Context

UK benefits and tax thresholds are typically uprated in **April** (fiscal year start), based on September CPI of the prior year. However, the current uprating system uses January 1 dates throughout.

## Current Implementation

1. **OBR indices** stored at January 1 dates (annual calendar year forecasts) in `yoy_growth.yaml`
2. **`create_economic_assumption_indices.py`** generates indices at January 1 dates (line 53: `f"{year}-01-01"`)
3. **`uprate_parameters`** in policyengine-core adds new parameter values at the same dates as the uprating index
4. **`convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters`** post-processes by sampling at April 30 and setting that as the year value

This works for annual simulations but has limitations:
- Intra-year queries don't reflect the actual April uprating date
- The fiscal year conversion is a workaround rather than correct modeling
- Parameters show January 1 dates in values_list even though actual policy changes April 6

## Ideal Approach

1. Store/generate uprating indices at **April 1** or **April 6** dates (representing fiscal years)
2. Uprating would then naturally produce values at April dates
3. Remove the fiscal year conversion post-processing step

This would:
- Be more accurate (uprating happens at the correct date)
- Eliminate the `convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters` workaround
- Handle mid-year policy changes correctly by default
- Allow specific date queries to work properly (e.g., `param("2026-03-15")` vs `param("2026-05-15")`)

## Implementation Notes

Would require changes to:
1. `policyengine_uk/parameters/gov/economic_assumptions/yoy_growth.yaml` - change dates from January 1 to April 1/6
2. `policyengine_uk/parameters/gov/economic_assumptions/create_economic_assumption_indices.py` - generate at April dates
3. Potentially `policyengine-core`'s `uprate_parameters` if any assumptions about January dates
4. Remove or modify `convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters` in `utils/parameters.py`

## Priority

Low - current approach works correctly for annual simulations after PR #1435 extended the fiscal year conversion range. This is an enhancement for more accurate intra-year modeling.

## Related

- PR #1435: Extended fiscal year conversion range to 2040
- Issue #1436: On-the-fly fiscal year conversion (alternative approach)

issues.title: Explore on-the-fly fiscal year parameter conversion
issues.body:
## Context
PR #1435 fixes the fiscal year parameter conversion range by extending it from 2015-2025 to 2015-2040. This is a simple fix but requires pre-computing values for all 26 years at startup.

## Proposed Enhancement
Explore converting fiscal year parameters on-the-fly rather than pre-computing them. This would:

1. **Remove the year range limit entirely** - No need to extend the range for future projections
2. **Potentially improve startup time** - No pre-computation needed for all years
3. **Simplify the code** - Just convert January 1 queries to April 30 dynamically

## Attempted Implementation
An initial attempt at this approach was made in PR #1434 by:
- Adding `convert_instant_to_fiscal_year()` function
- Overriding `get_parameters_at_instant()` in `CountryTaxBenefitSystem`
- Making `convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters()` a no-op

However, this broke 24 existing tests because it changed parameter lookup behavior for ALL dates, not just annual queries.

**PR #1434 contains the work-in-progress on-the-fly implementation** - it can be used as a starting point.

## Investigation Needed
- Understand why the on-the-fly approach broke existing tests
- Determine if on-the-fly conversion can be safely implemented
- Consider performance implications
- Evaluate backward compatibility concerns

## References
- PR #1435: Simple fix (extend range to 2040) ✅ 
- PR #1434: On-the-fly approach (work-in-progress implementation for this issue)

issues.title: Gift Aid donations not reducing ANI for Personal Allowance taper calculation
issues.body:
## Bug Description

Gift Aid donations are not being deducted from Adjusted Net Income (ANI) when calculating the Personal Allowance (PA) taper for high earners (£100k-£125k income).

Per [ITA 2007 s.58](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/58), Step 2:
> "If in the tax year the individual makes, or is treated under section 426 as making, a gift that is a qualifying donation for the purposes of Chapter 2 of Part 8 (gift aid) deduct the grossed up amount of the gift."

The grossed-up amount is defined as "the amount of the gift grossed up by reference to the basic rate for the tax year" (i.e., gift_aid / (1 - 0.2) = gift_aid * 1.25).

## Impact

High earners making charitable donations receive less tax relief than legally entitled:

**Example: £110k income + £10k Gift Aid donation**

| Metric | Before (Bug) | After (Fixed) |
|--------|-------------|---------------|
| ANI for PA taper | £110,000 | £97,500 (£110k - £12.5k grossed up) |
| Personal Allowance | £7,570 (tapered) | £12,570 (full) |
| Income Tax | ~£33,432 | ~£27,432 |
| Effective Relief | ~40% | ~60% |

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from policyengine_uk import Simulation

sim = Simulation(situation={
    "people": {"person": {"employment_income": {2025: 110000}, "gift_aid": {2025: 10000}}},
    "households": {"household": {"members": ["person"]}}
})

print(f"Personal Allowance: £{sim.calculate('personal_allowance', 2025)[0]:,.0f}")
# Expected: £12,570 (full PA restored as ANI for taper = £97,500 < £100k threshold)
# Actual: £7,570 (tapered, incorrectly using full £110k ANI)
```

## Root Cause

The `personal_allowance` variable uses `adjusted_net_income` directly without subtracting the grossed-up Gift Aid amount as required by ITA 2007 s.58.

## Proposed Fix

1. Create a `gift_aid_grossed_up` variable: `gift_aid / (1 - basic_rate)`
2. Modify `personal_allowance` to subtract `gift_aid_grossed_up` from ANI when calculating the PA taper

## Related Legislation

- [ITA 2007 s.58 - Meaning of "adjusted net income"](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/58)
- [ITA 2007 s.35 - Personal allowance](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/35)
- [ITA 2007 Part 8 Chapter 2 - Gift Aid](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/part/8/chapter/2)

issues.title: Gift Aid: Add legislation references and fix PA taper interaction
issues.body:
## Summary

The Gift Aid variable (`gift_aid`) is missing legislation references and the interaction with Personal Allowance taper is not correctly modeled.

## Current Implementation

The `gift_aid` variable in `variables/gov/hmrc/income_tax/allowances/gift_aid.py` has:
- No `reference` attribute linking to legislation.gov.uk
- No documentation of the relief mechanism

```python
class gift_aid(Variable):
    value_type = float
    entity = Person
    label = "Expenditure under Gift Aid"
    definition_period = YEAR
    unit = GBP
```

## Issues

### 1. Missing Legislation References

Gift Aid relief is governed by:
- [ITA 2007 Part 8 Chapter 2](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/part/8/chapter/2) - Gift Aid relief
- [ITA 2007 s.414](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/414) - Gift Aid relief: overview
- [ITA 2007 s.416](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/416) - Basic rate relief
- [ITA 2007 s.414(2)](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/414) - Higher rate relief via extension of basic rate band

### 2. Personal Allowance Taper Interaction (Bug)

**Current behavior:**
```
£110k income, £10k Gift Aid:
- Personal Allowance: £7,570 (unchanged)
- Tax savings: £4,000 (40% of £10k)
```

**Expected behavior:**
Per [ITA 2007 s.58](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/58), adjusted net income (ANI) should be reduced by the grossed-up Gift Aid amount when calculating PA taper.

For £10k net Gift Aid donation:
- Gross amount = £10,000 × 100/80 = £12,500
- ANI reduction = £12,500
- PA restoration = £6,250 (at £1 PA lost per £2 ANI over threshold)
- Additional tax relief from PA restoration at 40% = £2,500

This means effective relief in the taper zone should be ~60%, not 40%.

## Suggested Fix

1. Add `reference` attribute to gift_aid variable
2. Modify ANI calculation to subtract grossed-up gift aid before PA taper calculation
3. Add integration test for PA taper interaction

## Test Cases

```python
# Test PA taper interaction
situation = {
    "people": {"person": {"employment_income": {2025: 110000}, "gift_aid": {2025: 10000}}},
    ...
}
# Expected: PA should increase from £7,570 to ~£13,820
# Expected: Effective relief rate ~60%
```

issues.title: Add GitHub Actions workflow for Cloud Run deployment

## Problem
Currently, the backend deployment to Google Cloud Run must be done manually. There's no CI/CD automation for backend deployments when code is merged to master.

```bash
# Build and push Docker image
gcloud builds submit --tag gcr.io/ri-ctc-calc-2024/ri-ctc-calculator-backend:latest --project=ri-ctc-calc-2024

gcloud run deploy ri-ctc-calculator-backend \

  --project=ri-ctc-calc-2024 \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --platform=managed \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --memory=8Gi \
  --cpu=2 \
  --timeout=300
```

## Proposed Solution
Add a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml`) that:
1. Triggers on push to `master` branch when backend files change
2. Authenticates with GCP using Workload Identity Federation (preferred) or service account key
3. Builds and pushes the Docker image to GCR
4. Deploys to Cloud Run

## Requirements
- GCP service account with Cloud Run Admin and Cloud Build roles
- GitHub secret for GCP credentials (or Workload Identity setup)
- Path filter to only deploy when backend code changes

issues.title: Implement UK tax calculations
issues.body:
## Summary

Create UK-specific tax calculation functions similar to US `calculate_donation_effects()`.

## Implementation

Create `givecalc/uk/tax.py` with:

- `calculate_uk_donation_effects()` - Calculate tax impact across donation range
- `calculate_uk_donation_metrics()` - Calculate metrics at specific donation amount
- `create_uk_donation_dataframe()` - Build DataFrame with analysis results

## Key UK Tax Variables

- `income_tax`: Total income tax liability
- `household_benefits`: Total benefits received  
- `household_net_income`: Market income + benefits - taxes
- `gift_aid`: Charitable donations via Gift Aid

## UK Gift Aid Mechanics

Gift Aid provides tax relief in two ways:

1. **Charity reclaim**: Charity claims 25p per £1 donated (basic rate relief)
2. **Donor relief**: Higher/additional rate taxpayers claim additional relief

For a £100 donation by a 40% taxpayer:
- Charity receives: £100 + £25 (basic rate reclaim) = £125
- Donor claims: £25 (difference between 40% and 20% on £125 gross)
- Net cost to donor: £100 - £25 = £75
- Total charity benefit: £125
- Total government subsidy: £50 (£25 to charity + £25 to donor)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] TDD: Tests written first
- [ ] Correctly calculates UK income tax for various income levels
- [ ] Gift Aid donations reduce taxable income appropriately
- [ ] Marginal savings rate calculated correctly
- [ ] Higher rate relief shown for 40%+ taxpayers

issues.title: Fix slow cold start on Cloud Run (30+ seconds)
issues.body:
## Problem

GiveCalc takes 30+ seconds to load on first visit due to Cloud Run cold start. The container spins down after inactivity and takes a long time to restart.

## Root cause

The Docker container loads `policyengine-us` which is a large package. Cold start includes:
1. Container startup
2. Python interpreter initialization
3. Loading policyengine-us into memory

## Potential solutions

### Option 1: Keep one instance warm (recommended)
Set `min-instances: 1` in Cloud Run deployment.
- Cost: ~$15-30/month
- Eliminates cold start entirely

### Option 2: Scheduled pings
Set up Cloud Scheduler to ping the API every 5-10 minutes to keep it warm.
- Cost: Nearly free
- May still have occasional cold starts

### Option 3: Optimize container
- Use a slimmer base image
- Lazy load policyengine-us modules
- Pre-compile Python bytecode

### Option 4: Better UX during loading
- Show informative loading message ("Starting tax engine...")
- Cache states list in frontend to show UI faster

## Recommended action

Set `min-instances: 1` - the simplest and most reliable fix. Update in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:

```yaml
gcloud run deploy givecalc \
  --min-instances 1 \
  ...
```

Or via console: Cloud Run > givecalc > Edit > Minimum instances = 1

issues.title: Frontend build fails: missing lib/api.ts and lib/types.ts
issues.body:
## Problem

The frontend fails to build with the error:
```
Module not found: Can't resolve '@/lib/api'
```

This causes the \"Error calculating aggregate impact / network error\" message that users see when trying to use the calculator.

## Root Cause

The `frontend/lib/api.ts` and `frontend/lib/types.ts` files are referenced in the codebase but never existed:
- `frontend/hooks/useAggregateImpact.ts` imports from `@/lib/api`
- `frontend/hooks/useHouseholdImpact.ts` imports from `@/lib/api`
- Multiple components import types from `@/lib/types`

The README even documents these files as existing, but they were never created.

## Impact

- Frontend build fails completely
- Users see \"network error\" when trying to calculate aggregate impact
- The calculator is non-functional

## Solution

Create the missing files:
- `frontend/lib/api.ts` - API client with proper timeout handling (2 min for aggregate calculations)
- `frontend/lib/types.ts` - TypeScript types matching backend Pydantic models

issues.title: Add upper interest threshold freeze for Plan 2 (Budget 2025)
issues.body:
## Summary

Budget 2025 freezes BOTH interest rate thresholds for Plan 2 student loans from 2027-2030, but policyengine-uk only has values through 2026-09-01 and relies on RPI uprating thereafter.

Per [GOV.UK announcement](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/student-loans-interest-and-repayment-threshold-announcement-for-plan-2-and-plan-3-loans):
> "The income threshold and the **lower interest rate threshold** for repayment of Plan 2 loans to apply from April 2026 is £29,385."
> "The **higher interest threshold** for repayment of Plan 2 loans to apply from April 2026 is £52,885."

Per OBR EFO November 2025 (section 3.22):
> "The Government has announced a freeze to the repayments **and interest rate thresholds** for Plan 2 student loan repayments for three years starting from 2027-28."

## Current State

`interest_rates/plan_2/upper_threshold.yaml` ends at 2026-09-01 (£52,885) with RPI uprating - no frozen values for 2027-2029.

## Required Change

Add frozen values to `upper_threshold.yaml`:
```yaml
  2027-09-01:
    value: 52_885
    metadata:
      reference:
        - title: Autumn Budget 2025 - Student loans threshold freeze
          href: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2025-document/budget-2025-html
  2028-09-01:
    value: 52_885
  2029-09-01:
    value: 52_885
```

issues.title: Add upper interest threshold freeze for Plan 2 student loans
issues.body:
## Summary

The lifecycle calculator currently freezes the **lower** interest threshold (repayment threshold) for 2027-2029 but does **not** freeze the **upper** interest threshold as announced in Budget 2025.

Per OBR EFO November 2025 (section 3.22):
> "The Government has announced a freeze to the repayments **and interest rate thresholds** for Plan 2 student loan repayments for three years starting from 2027-28."

## Current Implementation

| Threshold | Frozen? | Current behavior |
|-----------|---------|------------------|
| Lower interest threshold (£29,385) | ✅ Yes | Frozen 2027-2029 |
| Upper interest threshold (£52,885) | ❌ No | RPI uprated from 2026 |

## Impact

The interest rate taper works as:
- Below lower threshold: RPI only
- Above upper threshold: RPI + 3%
- Between: Linear taper

By not freezing the upper threshold:
- Middle-income earners pay less interest than they should under the reform
- The taper band widens with inflation instead of staying fixed
- Underestimates the fiscal impact of the threshold freeze

## Required Changes

Add frozen upper threshold values for 2027-2029 in:
1. `backend/main.py` - `STUDENT_LOAN_INTEREST_UPPER_THRESHOLDS`
2. `frontend/index.html` - `INTEREST_UPPER_THRESHOLDS`

Upper threshold should be frozen at £52,885 (the 2026-09-01 announced value) through 2029.

issues.title: Impute student loan balance from WAS to FRS
issues.body:
## Summary

Add student loan (SLC) balance imputation from the Wealth and Assets Survey (WAS) to the FRS, following the same pattern as existing wealth imputations in `wealth.py`.

## WAS Data Available

Student loan balance can be derived from WAS Round 7 (April 2018 - March 2020):
- `Tot_LosR7_aggr` (total loans) minus `Tot_los_exc_SLCR7_aggr` (total loans excluding SLC) = SLC debt

### WAS Statistics
| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Unweighted households with SLC debt | 701 |
| Weighted households with SLC debt | 1.66m |
| Mean balance (those with debt) | £20,028 |
| Median balance | £14,000 |
| Max | £210,000 |
| Total weighted | £33.4bn |

### Comparison to Admin Statistics (~2019-20)
| Metric | WAS | Admin (SLC) |
|--------|-----|-------------|
| Borrowers/HH with debt | 1.66m HH | ~4.5m individuals |
| Total outstanding | £33.4bn | ~£140bn UK |
| Coverage | 24% | 100% |

WAS undercounts due to young graduate underrepresentation and household vs individual unit. However, it captures the **distribution shape** which is valuable for imputation.

## Implementation

1. Add to `wealth.py` RENAMES dict:
```python
"Tot_LosR7_aggr": "total_loans",
"Tot_los_exc_SLCR7_aggr": "total_loans_exc_slc",
```

2. Derive SLC debt in `generate_was_table()`:
```python
was["student_loan_balance"] = was["total_loans"] - was["total_loans_exc_slc"]
```

3. Add `"student_loan_balance"` to `IMPUTE_VARIABLES`

4. Consider scaling imputed values to match SLC admin totals (currently £267bn for England, March 2025)

## Why Needed

- FRS `student_loans` (`tuborr`) is amount borrowed THIS YEAR by current students, not outstanding balance
- 98.7% of FRS repayers have `student_loans = 0`
- Without balance data, we can't cap repayments at outstanding balance (high earners get unrealistic modelled repayments)
- Needed for interest accrual calculations

## Related Issues
- #237 - Add student loan repayment calibration targets
- policyengine-uk will need a `student_loan_balance` variable to use the imputed data

## Sources
- [SLC Statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/student-loans-company/about/statistics)
- [Student Loans in England 2024-25](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/student-loans-in-england-2024-to-2025)

issues.title: Add 2026 student loan interest rate thresholds and clarify uprating methodology
issues.body:
## Summary

The Plan 2 student loan interest rate thresholds (lower and upper) are missing the announced 2026 values and need clarification on uprating methodology for future years.

## Current State

The `policyengine_uk/parameters/gov/hmrc/student_loans/interest_rates/plan_2/` directory has:
- `lower_threshold.yaml`: Values through 2025-09-01 (£28,470)
- `upper_threshold.yaml`: Values through 2025-09-01 (£51,245)

## Missing Data

GOV.UK has announced the 2026-04 values:
- Lower interest threshold: £29,385 (same as repayment threshold)
- Upper interest threshold: £52,885

Source: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/student-loans-interest-and-repayment-threshold-announcement-for-plan-2-and-plan-3-loans

## Uprating Methodology Question

The Budget 2025 froze the Plan 2 **repayment threshold** at £29,385 from 2027-2030. The documentation in `lower_threshold.yaml` notes that "This is the same as the Plan 2 repayment threshold."

Questions:
1. Should the lower interest threshold also be explicitly frozen for 2027-2029 to match the repayment threshold freeze?
2. The upper interest threshold has no announced freeze - should it be set to use RPI uprating for future years?

## Historical Analysis

Looking at historical changes vs RPI:
- 2025: +2.9% (lower), +3.3% (upper) — closely matched RPI (~2.7%)
- 2026: +3.2% (lower), +3.2% (upper) — closely matched RPI (~3.2%)

When not explicitly frozen, the thresholds appear to track RPI reasonably well.

## Suggested Changes

1. Add 2026-09-01 values:
   - `lower_threshold.yaml`: £29,385
   - `upper_threshold.yaml`: £52,885

2. Add frozen values for lower threshold (2027-2029) to match repayment threshold freeze

3. Consider adding `uprating: gov.economic_assumptions.indices.obr.rpi` metadata to upper_threshold.yaml for years beyond the announced values

issues.title: Add student loan repayment calibration targets
issues.body:
## Summary

Add student loan repayment and balance calibration targets to the loss function using SLC (Student Loans Company) official statistics.

## Context

Currently, student loan repayments are not calibrated to external aggregates. Analysis shows PolicyEngine UK's modelled repayments are ~95% of FRS-reported values, but we should validate against official SLC statistics.

## Proposed Calibration Targets (from SLC 2024-25 statistics)

### Total Repayments by Country
| Country | Repayments | 
|---------|------------|
| England (HE) | £5.0bn |
| Scotland | £203m |
| Wales | £229m |
| Northern Ireland | £182m |
| **UK Total** | **~£5.6bn** |

### Repayments by Plan Type (England)
| Plan | Amount | Share |
|------|--------|-------|
| Plan 1 | £1.9bn | 37% |
| Plan 2 | £2.8bn | 55% |
| Postgraduate | £0.3bn | 7% |
| Plan 5 | £41m | 0.8% |

### Number of Borrowers Repaying (England)
- 3.0m via HMRC (39.5% of those liable)
- 187k scheduled direct to SLC
- 147k voluntary direct to SLC

### Outstanding Loan Balance
- UK Total: £294bn (March 2025)
- England: £267bn (March 2025)
- Projected peak: ~£492bn (2024-25 prices) / £863bn nominal in mid-2040s

## DfE/OBR Forecasts for Time Series Calibration

The DfE publishes detailed forecasts through 2073-74 that could be used for projecting calibration targets:

### Projected Outstanding Balance (Plan 1 only, declining)
| Year | Nominal | Real (2024-25) |
|------|---------|----------------|
| 2024-25 | £32.7bn | £32.7bn |
| 2025-26 | £31.3bn | £30.3bn |
| 2026-27 | £30.0bn | £27.9bn |
| 2027-28 | £28.7bn | £26.0bn |
| 2028-29 | £27.6bn | £24.3bn |

### Key Forecast Parameters
- **RAB charge** (write-off rate): 37% for 2026-27 cohort (reduced from 57%)
- **Average lifetime repayment**: £28,000 (2024-25 prices)
- **Repayment completion rate**: 56% of Plan 5 borrowers expected to repay in full
- **Borrower growth**: 512k→563k undergraduate entrants (2023/24→2029/30)

### Full Forecast Dataset
The DfE provides a comprehensive dataset with 850 rows covering 2024-25 to 2073-74, broken down by plan type:
- [Table 8: Projected long-term face value](https://explore-education-statistics.service.gov.uk/data-catalogue/data-set/d248b742-cbf8-4e10-b72d-0cc43e8e3959)

## Implementation Notes
1. Add targets to `loss.py` similar to existing benefit/tax targets
2. Consider timing alignment (FRS year vs SLC reporting year)
3. May need to decide whether to calibrate on modelled (`student_loan_repayment`) or reported (`student_loan_repayments`)
4. Plan-level breakdown would require `student_loan_plan` variable in calibration
5. For future years, use DfE forecasts to project calibration targets

## Sources

### Current Statistics
- [Student Loans in England 2024-25](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/student-loans-in-england-2024-to-2025)
- [Student Loans in Scotland 2024-25](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/student-loans-in-scotland-2024-to-2025)

issues.title: Add student loan interest rate parameters
issues.body:
## Summary

UK Plan 2 student loan interest rates vary with income, but policyengine-uk currently only has repayment parameters. We should add the interest rate rules to document the policy even if not actively used in simulations.

## Current Interest Rate Structure

### Plan 2 (2012-2023 undergraduates)
- While studying: RPI + 3%
- After course, income-dependent:
  - Income ≤ £27,296: RPI only
  - Income £27,296 - £49,130: RPI + tapered rate (0% to 3%)
  - Income > £49,130: RPI + 3%

### Plan 5 (from 2023)
- RPI only (no income-based component)

### Plan 1 and Plan 4
- Lower of RPI or Bank of England base rate + 1%

## Proposed Parameters

Add under `gov/hmrc/student_loans/interest_rates/`:
- `plan_1.yaml` - base rate + 1% cap
- `plan_2/base.yaml` - RPI base
- `plan_2/additional_rate.yaml` - the 0-3% addition
- `plan_2/lower_threshold.yaml` - £27,296
- `plan_2/upper_threshold.yaml` - £49,130
- `plan_4.yaml` - same as Plan 1
- `plan_5.yaml` - RPI only
- `postgraduate.yaml` - RPI + 3%

## References
- https://www.gov.uk/repaying-your-student-loan/interest
- https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/student-loans-and-interest-rates-faqs/

reviews.title: Optimise import and microsimulation init performance
reviews.body:
Three changes that together reduce `from policyengine_uk import Microsimulation; sim = Microsimulation()` time by ~40% (10.75s → 6.6s):

**Enum encoding** - replaced `np.select` with `np.searchsorted` for O(n log m) lookup instead of O(n*m), with cached sorted lookup arrays via `@lru_cache`

**empty_clone** - replaced dynamic type creation with `object.__new__()` which is ~33x faster for the 32k calls during parameter cloning

**Period/instant parsing** - added `@lru_cache` to `_instant_from_string` and `_period_from_string` to avoid repeated `strptime` calls for the same period strings (called ~20k times during fiscal year parameter conversion)

Remaining bottlenecks are mostly inherent to data loading (`astype` at 0.80s, HuggingFace dataset at 0.82s) rather than algorithmic inefficiencies.

reviews.title: Add G7 GovAI Grand Challenge application
reviews.body:
## Summary

Add draft application for Canada's G7 GovAI Grand Challenge (Rapid Solution Labs).

- **Deadline**: December 1, 2025 at 3:00 PM ET
- **Prize**: Up to $10,000 CAD (targeting 18-29 age category)
- **Team**: Nikhil Woodruff (CTO) + Pavel Makarchuk (Director of Growth)

## Why 18-29 Category

Strategic choice: dedicated youth prize pool likely has fewer production-ready AI systems competing. PolicyEngine's 100K+ users speaks for itself without needing CEO on the application.

## Why Apply

## Problem

  The `update-dependencies` workflow has been failing when trying to update dependencies for the `policyengine-apis-integ` package. The workflow fails
  with package resolution errors like:
- (in the CI) Distribution not found at: file:///home/runner/work/policyengine-api-v2/policyengine-api-v2/projects/policyengine-api-full/artifacts/clients/python
- (sometimes locally) Package metadata name policyengine_simulation_api_client does not match given name policyengine-api-simulation-client

## Timeline & Root Cause

This issue likely started after directory names in the integration were renamed . The integration package depends on locally-generated API clients that:
  1. Are stored in `artifacts/` directories (which are git-ignored)
  2. Don't exist in the CI environment unless explicitly generated (so packages unavailable for the newly generated directories)

## Proposed Solution

  Add the `generate-clients.sh` script execution before running `make update`. This ensures the required client packages exist when `uv lock --upgrade` attempts to resolve the integration package dependencies.

## Testing

  This fix has been validated locally by:
  1. Deleting all artifacts
  2. Running the generate-clients script
  3. Successfully running make update
  4. Confirming integration tests pass with generated clients

Since this is a scheduled workflow that runs in GitHub Actions, merging this PR will provide the definitive test of whether the fix resolves the issue in the CI environment.

reviews.title: Fix behavioral response calculations returning zero FTE impacts
reviews.body:
Fixes #1328

**Problem**

The behavioral response implementation in ```labour_supply.py``` was systematically returning zero FTE impacts despite valid policy reforms with significant income effects. This affected the accuracy of dynamic scoring for tax and benefit policy changes.

**Root Causes**

1. Simulation state corruption: ```sim.reset_calculations()``` was clearing all computed values, causing subsequent calculations like ```household_net_income``` to return NaN or £0
2. NaN propagation: Division by zero in wage calculations created NaN values that weren't properly handled, breaking elasticity calculations
3. Timing issues: Income changes were calculated after simulation state corruption occurred

**Solution**

- Removed ```sim.reset_calculations()```: Prevents simulation state corruption while still applying behavioral responses correctly
- Enhanced NaN handling: Added ```.fillna(0)``` and included np.nan in replacement list for wage calculations
- Pre-calculated income changes: Calculate income effects before any simulation modifications to avoid timing issues

**Impact**

- Behavioral responses now work correctly, showing realistic FTE impacts (e.g., 51,197 total FTEs for major reforms)
- All existing tests pass (569/569) - no regressions introduced
- Dynamic scoring functionality restored for accurate policy impact assessment

**Files Changed**

- ```policyengine_uk/dynamics/labour_supply.py``` - Core behavioral response fixes

## Summary
This PR fixes memory-related test failures in GitHub Actions by implementing an optimized batched test runner with proper memory management.

## Problems Solved
1. **Memory Issues**: Tests consuming excessive memory causing "Killed: 9" errors
2. **Memory Inefficiency**: Tests running out of memory in GitHub Actions
3. **Code Duplication**: Multiple batch runners with redundant code

## Solution: Optimized Batched Test Runner

### Key Features
- **Smart batching by folder**: Groups tests by state/folder to share data structures efficiently
- **Memory cleanup**: `gc.collect()` between batches prevents OOM
- **Configurable batching**: `--batches` parameter controls splitting
- **Clean code**: Consolidated into single utility

### Batching Strategy
- **Baseline**: 2 batches
  - Batch 1: All state tests (~5,638 tests) - share data structures efficiently
  - Batch 2: Federal/other tests (~2,034 tests)
  - Memory cleared between batches
- **Contrib**: Tests grouped by folder for optimal memory usage

## Changes
- ✅ Updated `test_batched.py` with folder-based batching for contrib tests
- ✅ Optimized memory usage by processing related tests together
- ✅ Updated GitHub Actions to run comprehensive tests with better visibility
- ✅ Split test runs into separate GitHub Actions steps for clearer output

## Testing
```bash
# Run all tests locally (same as GitHub Actions)
make test-yaml-no-structural  # Baseline (2 batches) + reform
make test-yaml-structural     # Contrib (folder-based batching)
make test-other              # Unit tests

# Run specific batch only
python policyengine_us/tests/test_batched.py policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline --batches 2
```

## Impact
- ✅ Fixes memory exhaustion errors
- ✅ Improved test organization and visibility in GitHub Actions
- ✅ More efficient memory usage through smart batching
- ✅ Reliable GitHub Actions runs
- ✅ Better test output clarity with separated test steps

prs.body:
Fixes #6893

## Summary

This PR corrects the Medicare Savings Program (MSP) implementation to align with federal statutory requirements. Key fixes:

1. **FPL Unit Size**: Uses individual/couple FPL instead of SPM unit size
2. **Income Methodology**: Applies SSI income exclusions per statutory requirement
3. **Parameter Updates**: Adds historical values and proper legal citations

---

## FPL Unit Size Fix

**Legal References**:
- [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - Income "determined under section 1382a" (SSI methodology)
- [SSA POMS SI 01715.010](https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501715010) - Specifies "individual" and "couple" resource limits

**Rationale**: MSP follows SSI methodology, which uses individual or eligible couple as the unit. SSI does not include children or other household members in the income/resource unit. Medicare.gov also publishes limits only for "Individual" and "Married couple" categories.

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `spm_unit_fpg` which calculated FPL based on the full SPM unit size (could be 3, 4, 5+ people).

**Fix**: Created `msp_fpg` variable that returns:
- Individual FPL (1 person) if unmarried
- Couple FPL (2 persons) if married

---

## Income Methodology Fix

**Legal Reference**: [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - "income (determined under section 1382a of this title)"

Section 1382a is the SSI income determination methodology ([42 U.S.C. § 1382a](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1382a)), which requires:
1. $20 general income exclusion (from unearned first)
2. $65 earned income exclusion
3. 50% of remaining earned income excluded

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `adjusted_gross_income_person` without any exclusions.

**Fix**: Updated `msp_countable_income` to use SSI income variables and apply the `_apply_ssi_exclusions()` function.

---

## Published Limits vs Our Approach

Medicare.gov publishes income limits that are approximately $20/month higher than raw FPL thresholds. This is because they include the $20 general exclusion in the threshold.

Our implementation applies the $20 exclusion to income instead:
- **Our approach**: `(income - $20) <= FPL`
- **Published approach**: `income <= (FPL + $20)`

These are mathematically equivalent.

---

## Income Limit Legal Citations

| Category | FPL % | Legal Reference |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| QMB | 100% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(i)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_i), [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)-(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) |
| SLMB | 120% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iii)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iii) |
| QI | 135% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iv)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iv) |

---

## Test Plan

- [x] All 19 MSP tests pass
- [x] Unit tests for `msp_fpg`, `msp_category`, `msp_eligible`, `msp_benefit_value`
- [x] Integration tests for complete eligibility pipeline
- [x] Tests document calculation methodology with inline comments

reviews.title: Medicare savings program
reviews.body:
Fixes #6893

## Summary

This PR corrects the Medicare Savings Program (MSP) implementation to align with federal statutory requirements. Key fixes:

1. **FPL Unit Size**: Uses individual/couple FPL instead of SPM unit size
2. **Income Methodology**: Applies SSI income exclusions per statutory requirement
3. **Parameter Updates**: Adds historical values and proper legal citations

---

## FPL Unit Size Fix

**Legal References**:
- [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - Income "determined under section 1382a" (SSI methodology)
- [SSA POMS SI 01715.010](https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501715010) - Specifies "individual" and "couple" resource limits

**Rationale**: MSP follows SSI methodology, which uses individual or eligible couple as the unit. SSI does not include children or other household members in the income/resource unit. Medicare.gov also publishes limits only for "Individual" and "Married couple" categories.

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `spm_unit_fpg` which calculated FPL based on the full SPM unit size (could be 3, 4, 5+ people).

**Fix**: Created `msp_fpg` variable that returns:
- Individual FPL (1 person) if unmarried
- Couple FPL (2 persons) if married

---

## Income Methodology Fix

**Legal Reference**: [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - "income (determined under section 1382a of this title)"

Section 1382a is the SSI income determination methodology ([42 U.S.C. § 1382a](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1382a)), which requires:
1. $20 general income exclusion (from unearned first)
2. $65 earned income exclusion
3. 50% of remaining earned income excluded

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `adjusted_gross_income_person` without any exclusions.

**Fix**: Updated `msp_countable_income` to use SSI income variables and apply the `_apply_ssi_exclusions()` function.

---

## Published Limits vs Our Approach

Medicare.gov publishes income limits that are approximately $20/month higher than raw FPL thresholds. This is because they include the $20 general exclusion in the threshold.

Our implementation applies the $20 exclusion to income instead:
- **Our approach**: `(income - $20) <= FPL`
- **Published approach**: `income <= (FPL + $20)`

These are mathematically equivalent.

---

## Income Limit Legal Citations

| Category | FPL % | Legal Reference |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| QMB | 100% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(i)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_i), [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)-(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) |
| SLMB | 120% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iii)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iii) |
| QI | 135% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iv)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iv) |

---

## Test Plan

- [x] All 19 MSP tests pass
- [x] Unit tests for `msp_fpg`, `msp_category`, `msp_eligible`, `msp_benefit_value`
- [x] Integration tests for complete eligibility pipeline
- [x] Tests document calculation methodology with inline comments

## Summary

Implements Illinois Medicaid Presumptive Eligibility (MPE) for pregnant women per [89 Ill. Admin. Code § 120.66](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/Ill-Admin-Code-tit-89-SS-120.66).

MPE provides temporary ambulatory prenatal care coverage to pregnant women while their full Medicaid application is processed. The program's purpose is to "encourage early and continuous prenatal care of low income pregnant women who otherwise may postpone or do without that care."

- Income limit: 200% FPL (using MAGI methodology per § 120.64)
- Available regardless of citizenship/immigration status
- Household size includes unborn children (via `current_pregnancies`)

### Not Modeled
- "No prior MPE this pregnancy" rule (administrative data, not observable from survey)

Fixes #6786

Implements eligibility determination for the Illinois Health Benefits for Persons with Breast or Cervical Cancer (BCC) program, which provides Medicaid-equivalent coverage for eligible women.

| Requirement | Variable | Description |

| **Age** | `il_bcc_age_eligible` | Under 65 years old |
| **Immigration** | `il_hfs_immigration_status_eligible` | US citizen or qualified noncitizen |
| **Insurance** | `il_bcc_insurance_eligible` | Not Medicaid eligible and no employer-sponsored insurance |

### Files Added

**Variables:**
- `il_bcc_eligible` - Main eligibility determination
- `il_bcc_age_eligible` - Age under 65 check
- `il_bcc_insurance_eligible` - Insurance coverage check
- `il_hfs_immigration_status_eligible` - Shared immigration status check (reusable across IL HFS programs)

**Parameters:**
- `gov/states/il/hfs/bcc/eligibility/age.yaml` - Maximum age (65)
- `gov/states/il/hfs/qualified_noncitizen_statuses.yaml` - Shared qualified noncitizen list

### Refactoring

Consolidated immigration status eligibility into a shared variable (`il_hfs_immigration_status_eligible`) and parameter file, now used by both BCC and HBWD programs.

prs.title: Add labor supply elasticity age heterogeneity
prs.body:
## Summary

  This PR re-adds the age heterogeneity feature for labor supply response elasticities that was previously reverted. This implements the multiplier approach for age-based
  differences in labor supply responses.

  ## Context

  - Original implementation: PR #6681 (v1.426.0, released 2025-10-28)
  - Reverted in: PR #6821 (to address potential issues)
  - This PR: Re-implements the same feature for further testing and evaluation

  ## Changes

  **Parameter Structure**:
  - Restores nested directory structure for elasticity parameters
  - Adds age threshold and multiplier parameters for income and substitution elasticities
  - Age threshold: 65 years
  - Multiplier approach allows different elasticities for people above/below threshold

  **Files Changed (16 total)**:
  - `parameters/gov/simulation/labor_supply_responses/elasticities/income/*` - Age-adjusted income elasticity params
  - `parameters/gov/simulation/labor_supply_responses/elasticities/substitution/*` - Age-adjusted substitution elasticity params
  - `variables/gov/simulation/labor_supply_response/*.py` - Updated variable formulas
  - Test files updated to reflect new structure

  ## Technical Details

  The age heterogeneity uses a multiplier approach where:
  - Base elasticity values are defined
  - Age threshold is set (default: 65)
  - Multiplier is applied for individuals above the threshold
  - This allows different labor supply responses for older vs. younger workers

  ## Testing

  ✅ System loads successfully
  ✅ Parameter structure verified
  ✅ All files restored from original implementation

  ## Purpose

  This draft PR allows for:
  1. Further testing of the age heterogeneity feature
  2. Evaluation of its impact on policy simulations
  3. Refinement before final merge decision

reviews.title: Optimize CI: Fix memory issues and add workflow concurrency
reviews.body:
## Summary

Fixes memory timeout issues in CI tests by splitting them into parallel jobs with isolated memory, plus adds workflow concurrency to save CI resources.

### Changes

**1. Enhanced `test_batched.py` with `--exclude` parameter**
- Works for both `policy/contrib` and `baseline` directories
- Usage: `--exclude states,congress` or `--exclude states`

**2. Split test jobs into parallel CI jobs**

| Job | Tests | Est. Time |
|-----|-------|-----------|
| `NonStructural-States` | baseline/gov/states (1,554 tests) | ~21 min |
| `NonStructural-Other` | baseline (excl states), household, contrib, reform | ~9 min |
| `Structural-and-Python` | contrib (excl states/congress) + pytest | ~21 min |
| `Structural-Heavy` | contrib/states + contrib/congress | ~21 min |

**3. Updated Makefile targets**
```makefile
test-yaml-structural          # contrib (excl states/congress)
test-yaml-structural-heavy    # contrib/states + contrib/congress
test-yaml-no-structural-states # baseline/gov/states
test-yaml-no-structural-other  # baseline (excl states) + household + contrib + reform
```

**4. Added workflow concurrency**
- New commits to the same PR automatically cancel in-progress CI runs
- Prevents wasting CI resources when pushing multiple commits quickly
- Each PR has its own concurrency group (different PRs run independently)

### Why This Helps

- Each CI job runs on a **separate runner with isolated memory**
- Previous bottleneck: Non-Structural job took **30 min** (70% was baseline/gov/states)
- New structure: All jobs complete in ~21 min (parallel)
- **Total CI time reduced from 30 min to ~21 min**
- Workflow concurrency saves CI quota by canceling stale runs

Fixes #6941

Per form instructions, the previous implementation incorrectly floored ALL income sources at 0 if negative. This PR updates the logic to only floor the specific income sources that the form explicitly says "If negative, enter 0":

**Lines that require flooring:**
- **Net business income**: `farm_income`, `self_employment_income`, `partnership_s_corp_income`
- **Net royalty or rent income**: `rental_income`, `farm_rent_income`

**Line with special rules:**
- **Capital gains**: Uses `loss_limited_net_capital_gains` which limits losses to $3,000 ($1,500 for MFS)

**All other income sources** (wages, interest, dividends, Social Security, etc.) are now added as-is without flooring, since the form does not indicate they should be zeroed if negative.

## Changes

- Updated `mi_household_resources.py` to selectively floor only business and rental income sources
- Added unit tests for negative business income and rental income flooring
- Added unit tests for capital gains loss limitation
- Added integration test from issue #6894 with large negative capital gains

The previous PR #6905 was closed due to persistent `uv.lock` synchronization issues between local Windows environment and CI Linux environment. This PR is created fresh from the latest master branch which already has the correct `uv.lock`.

reviews.title: Fix state_group enum usage in FPG parameter indexing
reviews.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a bug where three variables were using `state_group` (EnumArray) instead of `state_group_str` (string array) when indexing Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) parameters. This caused errors in the production simulation API.

### The Error

Users encountered the following error when running simulations:
```
Error computing household_net_income_including_health_benefits for your household: 
Invalid value(s) ['CA'] for enum StateGroup. Valid values are: ['CONTIGUOUS_US', 'AK', 'HI', 'GU', 'PR', 'VI']
```

### Root Cause

The issue stems from a recent change in `policyengine-core` (around 2025-12-03) that made enum validation stricter:

> "Invalid enum values now raise ValueError instead of logging a warning and returning index 0. This prevents silent data corruption when incorrect enum strings are passed to simulations."

Previously, policyengine-core would silently coerce invalid enum values by returning index 0 (the first enum value). This masked bugs where the wrong variable type was being used for parameter indexing. With the stricter validation, these latent bugs are now surfacing as errors.

### The Fix

Changed three locations to use `state_group_str` instead of `state_group`:

| File | Line |
|------|------|
| `ky_family_size_tax_credit_rate.py` | 19 |
| `wv_low_income_family_tax_credit_fpg.py` | 19 |
| `repeal_state_dependent_exemptions.py` | 423 |

### Why This Matters

- `state_group` returns an `EnumArray` with enum objects like `StateGroup.CONTIGUOUS_US`
- `state_group_str` returns a string array like `['CONTIGUOUS_US']`
- FPG parameters are indexed by string keys (`CONTIGUOUS_US`, `AK`, `HI`, etc.)
- When passing an `EnumArray` to parameter indexing, the new stricter validation in policyengine-core can reject it

### Test Updates

Updated tests to derive `state_group` from `state_code` rather than explicitly setting it, ensuring the full code path is exercised and similar bugs don't go undetected.

## Request for Review

**I'm not 100% sure if this is a complete fix.** I would appreciate insight from those who worked on the recent enum validation changes in `policyengine-core` to confirm:

1. Is using `state_group_str` (string array) the correct approach for parameter indexing?
2. Are there other places in the codebase that might have similar issues?
3. Should `EnumArray` types work with parameter indexing, or is converting to strings the expected pattern?

## Test Plan

- [x] Run `policyengine-core test` on `ky_family_size_tax_credit_rate.yaml` - 4 passed
- [x] Run `policyengine-core test` on `wv_low_income_family_tax_credit_fpg.yaml` - 4 passed  
- [x] Run `policyengine-core test` on `repeal_state_dependent_exemptions.yaml` - 5 passed

reviews.title: Add Oregon TANF Program
reviews.body:
## Summary
Implements Oregon TANF (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) program.

Closes #1460

---

## Oregon TANF Income Flow (per OAR regulations)

### Step 1: Gross Income

All earned and unearned income of the financial group.

---

### Step 2: Countable Income

OAR 461-140-0010 - Apply exclusions to get countable income:

- Child Support Disregard (OAR 461-145-0080(2)):
  - $50 per dependent child per month
  - Maximum $200 per household
  - Only applies to ongoing recipients (not initial applicants)
  - Only for child support paid through Oregon Child Support Program

Countable Income = Gross Earned + (Gross Unearned − Child Support Disregard)

---

### Step 3: First Eligibility Test

OAR 461-160-0100 - Compare countable income to Countable Income Limit:

| Need Group Size | Countable Income Limit |
|-----------------|------------------------|
| 1               | $345                   |
| 2               | $499                   |
| 3               | $616                   |
| 4               | $795                   |
| 5               | $932                   |
| +1              | +$172                  |

If Countable Income ≥ Limit → INELIGIBLE (stop here)

---

### Step 4: Adjusted Income

OAR 461-160-0160 - Apply the 50% earned income deduction:

Adjusted Income = Countable Income − (Gross Earned × 50%)

---

### Step 5: Second Eligibility Test

OAR 461-160-0100 - Compare adjusted income to Adjusted Income Limit:

| Need Group Size | Adjusted Income Limit |
|-----------------|-----------------------|
| 1               | $326                  |
| 2               | $416                  |
| 3               | $485                  |
| 4               | $595                  |
| 5               | $695                  |
| +1              | +$110                 |

If Adjusted Income ≥ Limit → INELIGIBLE (stop here)

---

### Step 6: ELI Alternative Test (for enrolled recipients with earned income)

OAR 461-155-0030(3) - Exit Limit Increase allows higher income threshold:

- Applies when: Currently enrolled in TANF AND has earned income
- ELI Limit = Payment Standard × 2
- If ELI applies: Only test Countable Income < ELI Limit (skip adjusted income test)

| Need Group Size | Payment Standard | ELI Limit |
|-----------------|------------------|-----------|
| 3               | $506             | $1,012    |
| 4               | $621             | $1,242    |
| 5               | $721             | $1,442    |

---

### Step 7: Benefit Calculation

OAR 461-160-0100 - For eligible families:

Benefit = Payment Standard − Adjusted Income

| Need Group Size | Payment Standard |
|-----------------|------------------|
| 1               | $339             |
| 2               | $432             |
| 3               | $506             |
| 4               | $621             |
| 5               | $721             |
| +1              | +$110            |

---

### Step 8: Minimum Benefit Check

OAR 461-165-0060(3) - If calculated benefit < $10, no payment is issued.

---

### Example: Family of 3 with $800/month earned income

1. Gross Income: $800 earned + $0 unearned = $800
2. Countable Income: $800 (no child support to disregard)
3. Test 1: $800 > $616 (countable limit) → FAIL standard test
4. ELI Test (if enrolled with earned income): $800 < $1,012 → PASS
5. Adjusted Income: $800 − ($800 × 50%) = $400
6. Benefit: $506 − $400 = $106/month

---

reviews.title: Medicare savings program
reviews.body:
Fixes #6893

## Summary

This PR corrects the Medicare Savings Program (MSP) implementation to align with federal statutory requirements. Key fixes:

1. **FPL Unit Size**: Uses individual/couple FPL instead of SPM unit size
2. **Income Methodology**: Applies SSI income exclusions per statutory requirement
3. **Parameter Updates**: Adds historical values and proper legal citations

---

## FPL Unit Size Fix

**Legal References**:
- [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - Income "determined under section 1382a" (SSI methodology)
- [SSA POMS SI 01715.010](https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501715010) - Specifies "individual" and "couple" resource limits

**Rationale**: MSP follows SSI methodology, which uses individual or eligible couple as the unit. SSI does not include children or other household members in the income/resource unit. Medicare.gov also publishes limits only for "Individual" and "Married couple" categories.

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `spm_unit_fpg` which calculated FPL based on the full SPM unit size (could be 3, 4, 5+ people).

**Fix**: Created `msp_fpg` variable that returns:
- Individual FPL (1 person) if unmarried
- Couple FPL (2 persons) if married

---

## Income Methodology Fix

**Legal Reference**: [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - "income (determined under section 1382a of this title)"

Section 1382a is the SSI income determination methodology ([42 U.S.C. § 1382a](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1382a)), which requires:
1. $20 general income exclusion (from unearned first)
2. $65 earned income exclusion
3. 50% of remaining earned income excluded

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `adjusted_gross_income_person` without any exclusions.

**Fix**: Updated `msp_countable_income` to use SSI income variables and apply the `_apply_ssi_exclusions()` function.

---

## Published Limits vs Our Approach

Medicare.gov publishes income limits that are approximately $20/month higher than raw FPL thresholds. This is because they include the $20 general exclusion in the threshold.

Our implementation applies the $20 exclusion to income instead:
- **Our approach**: `(income - $20) <= FPL`
- **Published approach**: `income <= (FPL + $20)`

These are mathematically equivalent.

---

## Income Limit Legal Citations

| Category | FPL % | Legal Reference |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| QMB | 100% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(i)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_i), [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)-(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) |
| SLMB | 120% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iii)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iii) |
| QI | 135% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iv)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iv) |

---

## Test Plan

- [x] All 19 MSP tests pass
- [x] Unit tests for `msp_fpg`, `msp_category`, `msp_eligible`, `msp_benefit_value`
- [x] Integration tests for complete eligibility pipeline

- **CO AMTI** = Federal AMTI less exemption + CO additions - CO subtractions
- **CO AMT** = max(0, tentative minimum tax - normal tax)

New variables:
- `co_amt` - Colorado alternative minimum tax
- `co_tentative_minimum_tax` - Tentative minimum tax (3.47% × CO AMTI)
- `co_alternative_minimum_taxable_income` - Colorado AMTI

Closes #2708

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests for all 3 new variables (6 tests total)
- [x] Verified CO AMT is included in `co_income_tax`

## TAXSIM Validation

Validated CO income tax against TAXSIM 35 for 2023:

| Income | PE (before credits) | TAXSIM | Difference |
|--------|---------------------|--------|------------|
| $50,000 | $1,590.60 | $1,573.03 | 1.1% |
| $100,000 | $3,790.60 | $3,815.31 | 0.7% |
| $250,000 | $10,390.60 | $10,549.22 | 1.5% |
| $500,000 | $21,472.00 | $21,747.57 | 1.3% |

**Notes:**
- PolicyEngine matches TAXSIM within 1-2% before refundable credits
- Final tax differs due to $800 CO sales tax refund (TABOR) that TAXSIM may not model
- CO AMT rarely triggers with standard income because the AMT rate (3.47%) is lower than the regular rate (4.4%)
- AMT only triggers when CO AMTI exceeds CO taxable income by ~27%, which typically requires specific AMT preference items (ISOs, private activity bond interest) not available in TAXSIM
- TAXSIM doesn't separately report state AMT

Sources:
- [Colorado DR 0104AMT](https://tax.colorado.gov/DR0104AMT)
